description:

CIET's coolant is the biphenyl/diphenyl-oxide eutectic - Dowtherm A and Therminol VP-1 are the same chemistry under two trade names. TUAS today carries its own Dowtherm/Therminol property path across many files under array_control_vol_and_fluid_component_collections/.

TASK: route v3's coolant properties through the coolprop fork rather than TUAS's own implementation, and CHECK THE TWO AGREE before switching - a property discrepancy would show up as a regression-test failure attributed to the array migration, which would waste debugging time on the wrong layer.

Do not write a new Therminol correlation. If the coolprop fork's coverage is short somewhere (temperature range, a property TUAS has that it lacks), report that gap rather than papering over it.
title: CIET v3 fluid properties: use the coolprop fork's Therminol, do not reimplement

description:
No steady-state two-phase pressure-drop validation exists for TampinesSteamArray / tampines::components::Pipe. Only the transient (Edwards-O'Brien) path is exercised.

Thom (1964) gives two-phase multipliers r2, r3, r4 for boiling water/steam tabulated by pressure; Martinelli & Nelson (1948) covers 0.1 MPa to critical. Both are steam-water-specific and recommended at secondary-loop pressures, unlike the air-water-rooted Lockhart-Martinelli (1949).

Per maintainer direction 2026-08-04, any ported correlation code lands as a MODULE under tampines/src/hem/ or beside TampinesSteamArray in openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/ — not a new crate.

Scope context: crates/tampines-steam-tables/docs/validation-scope-turbine-and-pipe.md section 4.1.
title: V&V: two-phase frictional pressure drop — Thom (1964) / Martinelli-Nelson (1948)

description:
MAINTAINER INSTRUCTION, 2026-08-13: 'pls move the advection terms to implicit by default... do for both OPCPFluidArray and TampinesSteamArray, but use outram-foam FVM::div.'

THE TWO SITES:
  TampinesSteamArray -- crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1639
      let conv_he = fvc::div(&self.phi, &self.he);   // explicit div(phi h)/V
  OPCPFluidArray -- crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/src/openfoam_algorithms/rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1306
      fvc::div_limited(&self.phi, &self.he, self.he_convection_scheme.limiter());  // explicit

Use crates/outram-foam-basic-lib/src/fv_operators/fvm/div.rs:61  pub fn div(phi: &SurfaceScalarField, psi: &VolScalarField) -> FvMatrix

WHY: the energy convection is explicit while MOMENTUM in the same files is already implicit
(fvm::div_vec at :1351 and :986 respectively). The explicit energy term imposes a hard CFL limit that
NO number of PIMPLE outer correctors can lift -- the corrector loop is a Picard iteration whose contraction
factor IS the cell Courant number, so above Co = 1 it diverges however many are used. Measured on the HTGR
steam generator: hot-side cells 0.625 m, gas ~11 m/s, Co ~0.23 at the 0.0125 s substep and ~1.8 at a 0.1 s
plant step. That Courant limit is the sole reason the SG must substep 8x per plant step (op-6eqe).

PREMISE CORRECTION -- READ THIS, IT CHANGES THE WORK:
The maintainer believed TUAS's FluidArray already does implicit advection. IT DOES NOT. Verified 2026-08-13:
mass_flowrate NEVER enters coefficient_matrix in
.../one_d_fluid_array_with_lateral_coupling/calculation.rs (zero occurrences); every advection term lands in
power_source_vector built from last-timestep enthalpies, and the code says so -- 'we also consider outflow
using previous timestep temperature' (:437). The matrix holds only thermal inertia (rho_cp V/dt), lateral
conductance, and axial conduction (:337, :425, :620).
SO THERE IS NOTHING TO PORT. This is new work, not a copy of an existing TUAS implementation.

THE LIMITER PROBLEM -- do not do a naive swap:
fvc::div_limited applies a nonlinear flux limiter (Upwind/Linear/VanLeer/Minmod via fvc::Limiter). A nonlinear
limiter CANNOT go into a linear matrix, so fvc::div_limited -> fvm::div is not a like-for-like replacement and
would silently drop boundedness on the OPCP side.
Standard treatment, and what should be implemented: IMPLICIT UPWIND in the matrix (fvm::div) PLUS DEFERRED
CORRECTION -- carry (limited - upwind) as an explicit source. Unconditionally stable because upwind dominates
the matrix, while the deferred part recovers the limiter's accuracy. The deferred term is still Picard, but
well-behaved.

SCOPE: crates/tampines-steam-tables and crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop only. Do NOT change TUAS FluidArray
(CIET-validated regression path) and do NOT touch outram-park-digital-twin-engine.

ACCEPTANCE:
  - Both arrays stable at Courant numbers above 1; demonstrate with a test that FAILS on the old explicit path.
  - Boundedness preserved on the OPCP side -- show the limiter still does its job via deferred correction.
  - Before/after accuracy on an existing case; report any degradation honestly.
  - 'by default' per the maintainer: implicit is the default path, not an opt-in flag.

SEQUENCING: this SUPERSEDES part of op-6eqe. That bead's 8-substeps-per-plant-step conclusion exists only
because advection is explicit. Once this lands, revisit the SG substep count -- it should drop, possibly to 1.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
SCOPE REDIRECTED by the maintainer, 2026-08-13: 'stop the Tampines steam array agent... let's make sure the OPCPFluidArray has the mode for implicit and explicit energy balance. as a selectable enum. I want you to redirect the opcp agent to implement this implicit mode.'

TampinesSteamArray is OUT of this bead. An agent had been started on it and was stopped before making any edits
(verified: crates/tampines-steam-tables has no changes beyond the unrelated f32 warning sweep). TUAS is also out --
'leave tuas alone do not correct it'.

WORK IS NOW: crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop only. The explicit path already exists
(rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1306, fvc::div_limited with the EnergyConvectionScheme limiter enum at :276). Add the IMPLICIT
mode alongside it, selectable, using outram-foam-basic-lib fvm::div (fv_operators/fvm/div.rs:61).

DESIGN POINT handed to the agent: EnergyConvectionScheme's own doc comment says it is 'enum dispatch over the flux
limiter lambda(r)'. Implicit-vs-explicit is a TIME/MATRIX treatment, orthogonal to limiter choice -- you can want
van Leer with either. Recommended a SEPARATE enum (e.g. EnergyBalanceMode { Explicit, Implicit }) over adding
variants to the limiter enum, which would make that enum's documentation untrue. The agent owns the call and must
justify it.

BOUNDEDNESS: a nonlinear limiter cannot live in a linear matrix, so fvc::div_limited -> fvm::div is not like-for-like.
Specified implicit upwind in the matrix PLUS deferred correction carrying (limited - upwind) as an explicit source.
This matters more than usual here because op-1fyp documents dispersive over/undershoots on an advected thermal front
as a real MEASURED defect in this very array -- dropping boundedness would regress a bug that was deliberately fixed.

VALIDATION VEHICLE -- CHECKED, and Edwards is NOT available here. crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop has no Edwards
blowdown test; its tests/ are EOS/property tests (water_reference, helium_reference, single_cv_and_flash, ...). The
code REFERENCES Edwards-O'Brien at :355, :563, :761, :1652 but that case lives in tampines-steam-tables, now out of
scope. The agent must find the in-crate transient tests for the equal-timestep baseline and BUILD the primary
acceptance case: a run at cell Courant number above 1 where the explicit mode FAILS and the implicit mode succeeds.
A case that passes under both proves nothing.

RELATED, and should be reconciled after this lands:
  op-1fyp (P2, still Todo) -- the limiter fix for THIS array. The code at :1306 now calls fvc::div_limited citing
    that bead, so it looks done; either close it or record what remains.
  TampinesSteamArray has the SAME unfixed defect: its energy convection at
    crates/tampines-steam-tables/.../rhoPimpleFoam/mod.rs:1639 is still bare fvc::div, i.e. central differencing,
    unlimited, on an advection-dominated equation. op-1fyp never covered it. Filed separately.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
DONE 2026-08-13, pushed (8e97330d; SG wired at 68e35551).
EnergyBalanceMode { Explicit, Implicit } on OPCPFluidArray, kept separate from the EnergyConvectionScheme limiter
enum because measurement showed the axes are independent: explicit UPWIND also diverges at Co >= 1.25 while implicit
VAN LEER survives, so stability tracks the time treatment and accuracy tracks the limiter.
Deferred correction preserves boundedness -- verified, not assumed: fvm_div_matches_explicit_upwind_divergence
compares (M*h - S) against V*conv_upwind, worst mismatch 0 W EXACTLY against a 575 W largest cell term.
Co > 1 evidence: overshoot past the boundary value as % of span -- Co 1.25 gives +135.14% explicit vs +0.10%
implicit; Co 2.00 gives +47539% vs +1.19%. Attribution isolated: pressure and velocity stay finite in every diverged
explicit run.
Honest cost: implicit is LESS accurate at low Courant ((u dx/2)(1+Co) diffusion against explicit (1-Co)), so the
crate default stays Explicit + van Leer and the SG opts in explicitly.
Used the crate's OWN vendored fvm::div rather than outram-foam-basic-lib's, because Cargo.toml:29 and
openfoam_algorithms/CLAUDE.md:16 both document that the crate deliberately has no such dependency, for
Android-buildability. Deviation from the original instruction, flagged and accepted.

title: OPCPFluidArray: selectable implicit energy-balance mode via outram-foam fvm::div
